children: Indian government bonds are likely to gain in early deals on Friday, tracking US Treasuries, but investors could be cautious as they await a fresh debt supply later in the day.
The benchmark 6.94% 2036 bond (IN069436G=CC) yield is expected to move between 7.23% and 7.29%, according to a private bank trader, after ending at 7.2543% on Thursday.
New Delhi will sell bonds worth 330 billion rupees ($3.54 billion), including the liquid five-year paper.
"There could be some opening gains but major moves are unlikely until the auction, with cutoff driving the moves later," the trader said.

US Treasury yields eased on Thursday as a sharp selloff in US equities pushed investors to buy safe-haven bonds amid concerns about the future of the AI buildout, which has been a boost to the economy.
The decline comes as the economic outlook is weakening, with traders expecting the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates by only 25 basis points in December.
Expectations of a 50-bp rate hike have eased to 3%, after rising as much as 14% earlier this week, according to the CME's FedWatch tool.

Meanwhile, the Brent crude contract continues to hover around $92 per barrel but the outlook remains sensitive to developments in the Strait of Hormuz and any extended disruption could tighten global supply conditions quickly.
For India, a major energy importer, this remains an important macroeconomic risk because higher oil prices can add pressure to the current account deficit, the rupee and domestic inflation.

The market has positioned for another Reserve Bank of India rate hike in early December, after India's retail inflation moved above the RBI's 6% upper tolerance threshold for the first time in two years.
Overnight index swap rates may see some receiving interest.
On Thursday, the one-year (INR1YMIBROIS=CC) rate ended at 6.51%, while the two-year rate (INR2YMIBROIS=CC) ended at 6.4850%. The liquid five-year (INR5YMIBROIS=CC) rate settled at 6.5075%.
